sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 27; Internal Quality Checks row 27 annotation on default sign-in)
.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r3/task/solution/app/src/{app.tsx,custom-editor.js,runtime.ts} and server.js (targeted greps: undo grouping, restore, dynamic-code refusal, document-edge keys)
evidence:
Criterion-to-requirement map built for all 3 gate, 40 functional, 6 polish and 3 visual criteria against instruction.md and the six notes. Most criteria trace to an explicit public sentence (e.g. two-space nesting ui.md:15, one-Undo paste ui.md:7, multi-caret burst ui.md:9, Replace current moves on ui.md:11, whole-file HTML error line behaviour.md:3, fresh budget after interaction behaviour.md:5, restore retry idempotence behaviour.md:13, focus return and unsaved marker ui.md:17). No sign-in is graded. Instances that grade something the brief does not require:

(1) CONFIRMED BY TEXT, blocking instance. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:371 (cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state, weight 2.0): "Undo, pressed once or twice depending on how the app groups typing, must then remove that character and the marker, returning exactly the draft as it was before the marker was typed." The brief explicitly permits the opposite: environment/instructions/ui.md:9 "A run of ordinary single-caret typing may be undone in one step or character by character, whichever you prefer." A character-by-character app needs marker-length+1 Undo presses, so two presses leave most of the marker and the criterion's stated bar is not met. The sibling criterion at judge.toml:128 correctly says "Press Undo repeatedly until", so the two are inconsistent. The golden groups typing (solution/app/src/custom-editor.js:566-575), so the scripted golden run cannot expose this.

(2) judge.toml:353 (cw_history_restore_retry): "with a second tab holding the fourth revision, save a fifth revision elsewhere and try a restore from the stale tab: it must be refused and the saved head must stay the fifth revision." behaviour.md:11 requires open tabs to learn of newer revisions within about five seconds and only protects an unsaved draft ("keep my draft; do not load the newer revision over my work"); behaviour.md:13 forbids only an old-revision restore overwriting a newer save. A conforming app whose clean tab adopts the newer head on refresh sends a restore based on revision 5, which legitimately creates revision 6 and retains 5 in history; the criterion fails it. The golden passes only because it keeps record.revision stale and shows a notice (app.tsx:82,141,152). The same criterion's "through the control the app offers for retrying it" can also be read as clicking Restore again, which is a new request that the brief says creates a new revision.

(3) judge.toml:317 (cw_dynamic_code_refused): each refused draft "must leave the control's last-good picture in the preview". security.md:5 requires only refusal "with clear feedback"; behaviour.md:5 ties last-good restoration to a run that "throws, is stopped or exceeds the five-second run budget". An app that blocks the call, reports the reason and lets the rest of the draft finish (or a judge fixture that catches the refusal) shows the new draft's picture and is failed on an unrequired leg.

(4) judge.toml:173 (cw_js_semantic_coloring): "the function name must look the same at its declaration and at its call." ui.md:13 requires function names at declaration and calls to be coloured distinctly from keywords and strings; it never requires identical treatment at both sites. A theme that distinguishes declarations from calls (both distinct from the other categories) is failed. The fail clause only names "styled at only one of the two places", so the bar and the fail clause differ.

Lower-confidence notes (professional default arguable, reported for completeness): (5) judge.toml:137 requires the current Find match to be "a real selection" confirmed by the line readout; ui.md:11 only asks for next/previous navigation with wrap. (6) judge.toml:326 asks the judge to record and re-read the record "identity"; integration.md:7 requires ids to survive but nothing requires the id to be displayed. (7) judge.toml:83 and :128 say move to the document end/start "with the keyboard"; ui.md:5 lists only arrows, Home and End, so a judge using Ctrl+End could fail an app without that shortcut (the golden implements it, custom-editor.js:780-785). (8) polish/judge.toml:32 requires textual feedback after a completed Run and a successful Save; ui.md:17 requires clear labels and an unsaved marker, not a success message. No configured judge run exists, so none of these is run-measured; the raw evidence index is scripted golden behaviour only.
counterexample: Conforming app: single-caret typing is undone one character at a time, as ui.md:9 allows. In cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state the judge types a five-character marker, waits for the library refresh, types one more character, then presses Undo twice as judge.toml:371 instructs. Four marker characters remain, the draft is not "exactly the draft as it was before the marker was typed", and the criterion (weight 2.0) fails although the refresh preserved the Undo history exactly as required. Second counterexample: a clean stale tab that refreshes its head to revision 5 and then restores revision 1 as revision 6 fails judge.toml:353 despite never overwriting a newer save.
suggested_fix: judge.toml:371: replace "pressed once or twice depending on how the app groups typing" with "pressed repeatedly until that character and the marker are gone (one step or character by character are both acceptable)" and fail only if Undo cannot get back to the pre-marker draft. judge.toml:353: make the stale restore deterministic (stale tab has an unsaved edit, or perform the restore before the tab can refresh) or accept either refusal or a new revision that keeps revision five in history; say the retry is the same request, not a second Restore click. judge.toml:317: drop the last-good-picture leg or state the refusal-ends-the-run rule in security.md. judge.toml:173: require both sites to be coloured as function names and distinct from the other categories, not identical. Optionally name the allowed keys in judge.toml:83/128 and soften the selection, identity and success-text wording in items 5, 6 and 8.
